#915. Hydrogen Derivatives Enable Cost-Effective Carbon Neutrality in China

Thank you for visiting nature.com. You are using a browser version with limited support for CSS. To obtain the best experience, we recommend you use a more up to date browser (or turn off compatibility mode in Internet Explorer). In the meantime, to ensure continued support, we are displaying the site without styles and JavaScript.

Nature (2026) Cite this article

We’re sharing this article early to provide faster access to peer-reviewed, accepted research. It is citable and carries a permanent DOI. This version is subject to further edits and will be replaced automatically by the final Version of Record. All legal disclaimers apply.

The Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change recommended 1.5°C carbon reduction target, requiring powerful enforcement from major economies. China, the largest CO2 emitter, is facing severe difficulties for both variable renewable accommodation and decarbonization of hard-to-abate sectors. Hydrogen, as a critical green energy carrier bridging renewable to end-users, faces significant obstacles in real-world deployment such as costly transportation, storage and fuel-cell adoption. Affordable and coordinated hydrogen deployment plan to accelerate the carbon-neutral transition remains ambiguous. Here, we present cost-effective carbon-neutral transition pathways for entire energy economy of China emphasizing the significant role of hydrogen and derivatives as green energy carriers, considering high-resolution renewable deployments, hourly power system operations in 29 provincial regions, over 46,000 rail/road/marine/pipeline transfer routing of hydrogen derivatives, process-level fuel adoption strategies in all end-use sectors. Results show that incorporating hydrogen and derivatives can reduce the overall transition cost by $ 10.7 trillion compared with renewable and electrification pathways, achieving negative carbon abatement costs ($-6.15/ton), eliminating external oil import expenses, equivalent to over 50% of China trade surplus (2023 level)1, significantly boosting employment and economic growth. Hydrogen derivative based transition pathway offers a vital direction for affordable and secure decarbonization for China and beyond under volatile international energy markets.

#914. Transfer window verdict: how every Premier League club fared

The British transfer record was equalled and one club signed no fewer than 18 players in another hectic summer

Julián Alvarez made clear he had no intention of joining from Atlético Madrid in the final days of the window and Arsenal kept their powder dry despite sanctioning the exits of Gabriel Jesus to Barcelona and Ethan Nwaneri to Borussia Dortmund. Should Gabriel Martinelli complete his move to Al-Hilal as expected in the coming days – the Saudi Pro League window remains open – a few injuries could leave Arteta short. Ed Aarons

It is all change at Villa and, although a little trepidation is inevitable, a refresh was probably overdue. At the same time, Unai Emery did not want to lose so many key players and Villa’s manager has made clear there is no such thing as a transition season in his eyes. Villa have generated about £300m from the sales of nine players and brought in 10 at a cost of about £250m. Villa have lowered their wage bill and changed the profile of their squad. Zion Suzuki, Ibrahim Mbaye and Johan Manzambi, names on the lips of Villa’s rivals, are particularly exciting signings. Last summer there was concern Villa had gone stale and 12 months ago they ended up fretting on deadline day – Harvey Elliott and Jadon Sancho joined on loan – but there was no such chaos this time. Ben Fisher

Perhaps Bournemouth’s best business was keeping hold of their coveted key players, chiefly Eli Junior Kroupi, Rayan, Alex Scott and Tyler Adams. Bournemouth rejected bids from Chelsea for Scott and stayed true to their plan of resisting offers to give Marco Rose the best chance of succeeding, with the club attempting to juggle European competition and the league for the first time. The arrival of the Portugal centre-back António Silva, 22, from Benfica looks a typically smart replacement for Marcos Senesi, 29. Kroupi’s freak foot injury, which will probably keep him out until November, may have proved a blessing in disguise in terms of retaining the 20-year-old. BF

Avoiding a repeat of last year’s upheaval was a major boost. Keith Andrews held on to his best players and made smart additions to a solid squad. Mamadou Sangaré has added quality in midfield since joining from Lens and looks the bargain of the summer. Callum Wilson has brought experience up front after signing on a free and Jaidon Anthony provides cover on the flanks after his £15m move from Burnley. El Hadji-Malick Diouf, signed from West Ham, offers potential at left-back. Jacob Steinberg

Key ins: Mamadou Sangaré (Lens, £39m), El Hadji Malick Diouf (West Ham, £35m), Jaidon Anthony (Burnley, £15m), Jannik Schuster (Red Bull Salzburg, £14m), Callum Wilson (West Ham, free)

Key outs: Ethan Pinnock (Coventry, £6m), Jordan Henderson (Chelsea, free)

Deadline day deals to bring in the exciting Nigeria forward Femi Azeez from Millwall and the Spanish midfielder Chema Andrés from Stuttgart made it 12 signings in another summer of transition, Azeez’s arrival being announced almost 12 hours after the window shut. The departures of Jan Paul van Hecke, Carlos Baleba and Carl Rushworth brought in more than £140m as the Brighton model continues to deliver big profits, although losing last season’s top scorer, Danny Welbeck, to Chelsea for a mere £5m may be the biggest loss if the new striker Promise David cannot bring the goals. EA

Xabi Alonso’s appointment as manager was the biggest signing of the summer. Chelsea have been sensible since turning to the Spaniard. Morgan Rogers has started well after joining for £117m. Maxence Lacroix adds power in defence, Marco Palestra versatility on the flanks. Danny Welbeck and Jordan Henderson can raise standards in the dressing room. But there was the usual revolving door. Money was made on a host of outgoings. Marc Cucurella, one of the world’s best left-backs and sold to Real Madrid, looks a bigger loss than Enzo Fernández. However a worry is that Chelsea did not replace Fernández after selling him to Manchester City for £125m, their late £47m move for Monaco’s Lamine Camara collapsing at the last. JS

It remains to be seen whether Coventry have struck the right balance in the market. Frank Lampard wanted to maintain momentum but add power and physicality. Coventry also sought to address their lack of Premier League experience with Taiwo Awoniyi and Ethan Pinnock. Coventry were the highest scorers in English football’s top four tiers last season but the step up means the pressure is on Awoniyi, never prolific for Nottingham Forest, Sidiki Cherif, a promising 19-year-old, and Ellis Simms to deliver before Haji Wright returns from injury. Stephen Mfuni, a teenage loanee from Manchester City and their 11th and final summer signing, increases their left-back options. BF

The lost tug of war with Sunderland over Malick Fofana summed up another chaotic deadline day for Palace, who were still scrambling for signings in the final minutes and confirmed the arrivals of Ben Chilwell, Quinten Timber and Darío Osorio after the window shut. The new manager, Pierre Sage, will at least be pleased to have secured more defensive reinforcements after losing Maxence Lacroix to Chelsea, with the loanees Honest Ahanor and Axel Disasi adding much-needed depth. Palace also kept hold of Ismaïla Sarr – presuming he doesn’t join a club in Saudi Arabia before the Sunday deadline there – after rejecting an approach from Liverpool for the Senegal forward. EA

It was a window that revealed the extent of The Friedkin Group’s ambitions, the strength of the club’s finances after the move to a new stadium, the state of the relationship between the manager and chief executive and the expertise of the senior leadership team; and none of it was positive. The owners deserve some credit for listening to fans and halting the self-defeating sale of Harrison Armstrong to Nottingham Forest but otherwise it was a modest window that descended into a shambles. The club’s best player was sold for a below-market fee, a move for Folarin Balogun collapsed and although the equally desperate search for a right-back ended with Ainsley Maitland-Niles signing, David Moyes was left with one striker and a smaller squad than he started the day with, despite repeatedly urging his employers to strengthen. AH

It was a summer of change at Craven Cottage. Marco Silva departed after five successful years in charge and was replaced by the inexperienced Álvaro Arbeloa, who has focused on adding youth. Gonzalo García, César Palacios and Manuel Ángel followed Arbeloa from Real Madrid and Shea Charles is an exciting signing from Southampton. Some stalwarts have left. Raúl Jiménez joined Wolves and Harry Wilson went to Leeds. Fulham looked to strengthen. They secured the midfielder Hugo Larsson and centre-back David Affengruber on deadline day but missed out on another target, the right-back Andrei Ratiu. JS

“Think of us like a volcano,” said Hull’s owner, Acun Ilicali, in early July. “It’s boiling right now and it’s going to erupt.” Two months on the Ilicali has presided over 18 signings, investing more than £150m and his manager, Sergej Jakirovic, has choreographed two Premier League wins. The horizon looks infinitely brighter than in June, when the playoff winners sold two players for a combined £8.5m to avoid breaching English Football League spending rules and a near-certain six-point deduction. Hull, remember, spent last season under a two-window EFL transfer embargo. They have compensated for that this summer and, although time will tell whether all those new faces are compatible, reasons for optimism remain real. Not least because last season’s cult hero loanee forward Joe Gelhardt has signed permanently from Leeds. Louise Taylor

The late addition of Burnley’s striker Zian Flemming brought Ipswich’s summer spend close to £200m. That appears to be the cost of giving yourselves a genuine shot at survival. Arrivals such as Exequiel Palacios and Julio Enciso should have no business in the lower reaches, and the former Fulham pair Sasa Lukic and Issa Diop add crucial experience. Gary O’Neil can call upon enviable depth in midfield and speed on the flanks, where Abdul Fatawu and Daizen Maeda look sharp. But time will tell whether Ipswich strengthened their defence sufficiently for regular tests of the kind they failed at Old Trafford on Sunday. Nick Ames

In an ideal world Daniel Farke might have wished for one more high-calibre attacking recruit but that should not detract from a very decent window, featuring seven extremely sensible signings. The importance of the acquisition of the England goalkeeper James Trafford from Manchester City should not be underestimated. Trafford will almost certainly provide Leeds with a few more extra points – not to mention enhance their play courtesy of his stellar footwork. Just in front of him Tarik Muharemovic looks an outstanding defensive buy. Harry Wilson raises creativity levels and the attacking tone. LT

The final window of Richard Hughes’s spell as sporting director raised more questions over Liverpool’s direction under Fenway Sports Group, owners soon to be enriched by a £2bn investment from 1892 Holdings. The shift towards paying big money for big names continued with Bradley Barcola’s arrival from Paris Saint-Germain while Jérémy Jacquet and Victor Muñoz followed the older policy of developing young potential. Yet weaknesses remain at right back, defensive midfield and on the right wing, where Mohamed Salah’s exit was foreseen from December. Squad depth is lacking and a lot rests on the return to full fitness of Hugo Ekitiké, Conor Bradley and Giovanni Leoni. AH

With Enzo Fernández’s deadline day signing for a British record-equalling £125m, Enzo Maresca can have zero complaints about a first window as Manchester City’s head coach. The No 8 follows two No 6s, in Elliot Anderson (£116m) and Ayyoub Bouaddi (£85m), and the wide players Allan Elias (£34m) and Iliman Ndiaye (£60m plus £5m) as major signings, the total spend on incomings about £457.5m. Factor in how City have generated about £281.8m in outgoings for a net spend of £175.7m, the divisions third-biggest of the window, and this sizable investment has to work - particularly the acquisition of Fernández. Jamie Jackson

Bernardo Silva (Real Madrid, free)

This was the window of the midfielder for Manchester United, with three recruited: Youri Tielemans (a No 8), Andrey Santos and Carlos Baleba (No 6s). Yet missing was a left-back despite the targeting of Lewis Hall, and others, plus reinforcements for the rest of a creaking rearguard. The reason? A lack of money or, maybe, a reluctance to spend unless the finance was generated by transfers. Manuel Ugarte’s long-term injury (preventing his sale) and Joshua Zirkzee’s reluctance to move were factors. Will the specialist Luke Shaw, plus the stand-in options of Parick Dorgu (a wing-back/left forward), Diogo Dalot and Noussair Mazraoui (right-backs), Lizandro Martínez (centre-back) and Baleba prove adequate? JJ

Newcastle describe their transfer window as “transformative” and, with reinvention the name of the game on Tyneside, it is easy to see why. After selling Anthony Gordon, Sandro Tonali and Bruno Guimarães for a grand total not too far off £250m, they have signed eight – mainly young – players. Along the way the spine of a team now managed by Matthias Jaissle rather than Eddie Howe has been renewed and new cult heroes including the former Benfica right-back Amar Dedic and the former Manchester City midfielder Nico González are emerging. The deadline day arrival of the exciting 21-year-old Belgium forward Matias Fernandez-Pardo from Lille is regarded as quite a coup. Have Newcastle choreographed a triumph from a window that, at one point, looked potentially disastrous? LT

Receiving £116m for Elliot Anderson was proof that among the chaos in recent years, Forest have carried out some smart recruitment. After appointing Oliver Glasner, the club worked to provide for his needs, splashing out on Ousmane Diomande, while Xaver Schalger was a sensible acquisition for free, as was Daniel Muñoz at £22m. A No 9 was the priority and it required a club record £45m to acquire the long-term target Liam Delap, who fits the bill perfectly. Whether not sourcing a direct replacement for Anderson will hurt them remains to be seen but at least they did not panic, making it a measured window where they were able to trim the squad. Will Unwin

After last summer’s 14 new faces this had been a bit of a conservative, almost slightly underwhelming, window. Or at least it was until Crystal Palace tried to hijack Sunderland’s agreement to sign the Lyon winger Malick Fofana and the two Premier League clubs engaged in an astonishing deadline day tug of war involving private jets from both sitting on the tarmac at Lyon airport and Fofana undergoing a medical in France unsure as to his destination until finally choosing Wearside. Arguably Sunderland’s biggest achievement was keeping last season’s star players. If persuading Granit Xhaka to stay rather than defect to Chelsea was vital, Régis Le Bris will be similarly delighted to have retained widely admired individuals of the calibre of Enzo Le Fée, Robin Roefs and Noah Sadiki. LT

A comprehensive reboot, from back to front, featuring a club record outlay for a window and one of the most lavish by any club ever. In the first summer window since the departure of the longstanding chair Daniel Levy, the hierarchy have backed Roberto De Zerbi in an attempt to put the trauma of last season behind them. All the new signings have Premier League experience and – apart from Mateus Fernandes and Sávio – are aged 25 or over. In other words, they ought to be ready to hit the ground running. The opening two matches did not go to plan. It will get better. Won’t it? David Hytner

It should be quite an atmosphere at the Metropolitano as Atletico Madrid take on champions Barcelona, who are two points ahead of them at the top of La Liga.

Atleti have been in scintillating form in the league, winning seven successive games to start the weekend sandwiched between Barca and their city rivals Real Madrid. They have already beaten one of the El Clasico heavyweights here this season, seeing off Real 2-1 in September, and will believe they can repeat the trick tonight.

Diego Simeone will want a reaction from his team after they lost 2-0 to Bayern Munich at the Metropolitano in the Champions League in midweek, a result that ended their unbeaten home record this term.

The return of midfielder Johnny Cardoso means centre back Cristian Romero is Atleti's only absentee, as they hunt a first home league victory over Barca since October 2021.

Barcelona have been in imperious form this season and beat Aston Villa 3-0 in the Champions League in midweek, but Hansi Flick's side still have a point to prove.

Their only two defeats of the campaign came against Paris Saint-Germain in the Champions League and Real Madrid in La Liga, so despite racking up 13 wins and 60 goals in all competitions, they are yet to claim a statement victory.

That would change if they take all three points at the Metropolitano and Barca know what it takes to achieve that, having already beaten Atleti twice in Madrid in 2026.

However, they have already suffered a setback after influential midfielder Rodri injured his hamstring against Villa, ruling him out of the visit to his former club. Of the other injured players, Andreas Christensen, Eric Garcia and Jules Kounde appear to be closest to returning, with Dani Olmo, Roony Bardghji and Xavi Espart longer-term absentees.

We expect Barca to edge a closely-fought contest thanks to their extra attacking quality.

James Roberts is a freelance sports journalist working for FourFourTwo and other titles. He started his career at the Oxford Mail, where he covered Oxford United home and away, before becoming a sports sub-editor for various national newspapers.

#910. Villa boss Emery explains why he went down tunnel before full-time

Unai Emery headed down Old Trafford tunnel before full-time after Man Utd rescued a 4-4 draw against his Aston Villa team; Patrick Dorgu scored late equaliser in thrilling contest; Villa director of football operations Damian Vidagany questioned legitimacy of last goal

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player

A prickly Unai Emery claimed he headed down the Old Trafford tunnel after Manchester United's late equaliser against his Aston Villa side because he thought the match was about to end.

Villa threw away two separate two-goal leads to draw 4-4 with United in a Super Sunday thriller - but the 97th-minute equaliser from Michael Carrick's side, scored by Patrick Dorgu, brought about a strange reaction from Emery.

The Villa manager was seen walking down the tunnel before the full-time whistle, with the match continuing for another two minutes before it ended.

Villa have complained about the legitimacy of United's fourth goal - with United goalkeeper Senne Lammens accused of impeding with Villa counterpart Zion Suzuki as he competed with Dorgu for the corner.

Asked if Emery walking down the tunnel was due to the emotional about the goal standing "No emotion. They scored in minute 96 and there were six minutes added. I [thought] the match was finishing."

When asked if he felt the goal being awarded was unfair, Emery replied: "No, no. Not unfair. Please.

"They scored the goal in minute 96. You were making the question [about why] I left before. Because the minute 96 and 30 seconds, was when we started the kick-off."

Sky reporter Patrick Davison: Does today happen because you're a new team or young side? It is an experience they have to learn from?

PD: Does history play a part, we spoke before the match that Aston Villa don't have a good record here.

UE: "We are in our way and we might be positive, even with this defeat [draw]. We have to be moving on with the process we have."

PD: Last one Unai, we saw you left before the end while VAR were...

UE: "No emotion. They scored in minute 96 and there were six minutes added. I think the match was finishing."

PD: You brought something up that I wasn't expecting. Did you think the goal was unfair?

UE: "They scored the goal in minute 96. You were making the question [about why] I left before. Because the minute 96 and 30 seconds, was when we started the kick-off.

"My English is so poor, but it's clear or not?"

UE: "Ok. Thank you, thank you very much. More questions?"

UE: "No? Thank you very much. Have a good Sunday."

Villa's director of football operations Damian Vidagany took to social media to show his dismay at United's last-gasp equaliser against his team being allowed to stand.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player

United goalkeeper Lammens - who went up for the corner - made contact with Suzuki whilst not looking at the ball, which left Villa furious. VAR checked and cleared Lammens' involvement in the goal.

Sky Sports' Roy Keane says "football is a contact sport" which means the goal should be allowed to stand.

However, Vidagany posted on X: "To put in context this convenient narrative of 'contact sport' we've been told by referees during the summer that this season to go to unbalance or push the GK on purpose on the six-yard box was not going to be allowed anymore.

"Lammens did not even look at the ball, went straight to do a contact with the hip over Zion.

"Having said that we played good match and we must do better than last six minutes. We will do and we will improve.

"But the rules are the rules and must be respected. That is a fact."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player

Emery admitted his anger at seeing Villa throw away their significant advantages at Old Trafford - but revealed his anger was not directed at his players.

"Angry, of course," he said in his press conference. "To accept to lose in the last minutes two goals, it is difficult.

"I am angry for the situation, not with the players. We lost the opportunity to have two points more."

Asked how United were allowed to come back into the game, Emery replied: "They did the same here against Roma with the supporters pushing, they were playing with heart.

"The last moments when we were close to finishing the match, with [Patrick] Dorgu left side, we couldn't defend him good.

"The last corner we were focusing on the adaptation, protecting them to try to avoid the block. Zion [Suzuki] is going to improve, adapting to the Premier League, but during the process we conceded one more.

"But Zion is very fantastic how he is performing."

#909. Germany's Merz says erosion of global order means middle powers in Europe and Asia must be more assertive

During a visit to Singapore, German Chancellor Friedrich Merz said Europe and Germany want to increase free trade with open competition, reliability and a rules-based order.

This blog is now closed. Below is a roundup of the top stories in Germany on Tuesday, October 27, 2026:

Don't want to miss our real-time updates? Click here to add us as a Preferred Source on Google.

Thank you for joining our coverage of German news on Tuesday.

We look forward to bringing you the latest again on Wednesday in a fresh blog.

On the first day of his farewell tour in China, German President Frank-Walter Steinmeier urged the German business community to act with confidence in the Chinese market.

"When you travel in China, you're amazed at how highly Germany and German technology are still valued here," he said in Hefei. "That's why we can act with confidence in these markets."

Steinmeier did not bring any companies with him to China as part of his delegation, as his final trip was intended to focus on culture and science.

Nevertheless, the first day of the trip in Hefei, the capital of Anhui Province, revolved primarily around the economy. Steinmeier visited the Volkswagen China Technology Company (VCTC). About three years ago, Europe's largest automaker opened a research center for electric mobility there, which today employs 3,000 people.

Johannes Volkmann, a lawmaker accompanying Steinmeier in China, warned that the German economy must not "lose its leadership in innovation."

"I'm taking this call to action with me from here to do more to improve competitive conditions at home," he said, adding that Germany must avoid creating new dependencies "by allowing innovation and value creation to take place only outside Europe."

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

Steinmeier called for Europe to reposition itself and reorganize its economic instruments with its growing trade deficit with China in mind.

"The trade surplus that China is accumulating naturally causes us concern because the successful model of economic cooperation is becoming unbalanced," he said. "We must strive to ensure that economic cooperation does not come to an end, but that it continues — to the mutual benefit of both sides."

Germany's trade deficit with China amounted to just under €90 billion ($100 billion) in 2025. According to the Federal Statistical Office, China exported goods worth €170.6 billion to Germany, and German exports to China amounted to €81.3 billion.

Across the 27-member EU, the deficit amounted to almost €197 billion in the first half of 2026, according to EU Trade Commissioner Maros Sefcovic.

Additional reporting by Rosalia Romaniec in Hefei.

A German court denied a defense request to end the trial of a former Ukrainian army officer who stands accused of sabotaging the Nord Stream gas pipelines.

Serhii Kuznietsov, 50, went on trial this month at the Hamburg state court, charged with causing an explosion, damaging property, disrupting public services and being an "accomplice to war crimes" by attacking civilian infrastructure.

Prosecutors accuse him of being the ringleader of the destruction, considered one of Europe's biggest acts of post-World War II sabotage. He is alleged to have carried out the explosions together with six others.

His lawyers said the charges should be dismissed, arguing that, as a former soldier, Kuznietsov was obligated by Ukrainian law not to speak for national security reasons and could face severe penalties in Ukraine if he did. They argued that, under German law, anyone who cannot speak on his or her own behalf cannot be convicted.

The Hamburg court ruled Kuznietsov's defense was not limited under German law and that freedom to testify is not limited by a foreign country's conditions of service.

The undersea explosions on September 26, 2022, damaged the Nord Stream 1 pipeline, which brought Russian natural gas to Germany until Moscow cut off supplies in August 2022.

The blasts also damaged the Nord Stream 2 pipeline, which never went into service. Germany suspended the pipeline's certification process shortly before Russia’s full-scale invasion of Ukraine in February 2022.

Italian authorities detained Kuznietsov last year. He was publicly named in extradition proceedings that led to his transfer to Germany in November.

Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy has denied allegations that his country was involved in the pipeline blasts.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

German carmaker Mercedes-Benz has cut its forecast for 2026, with difficult market conditions in China and higher fourth-quarter cost expectations set to negatively impact profits, the company said on Tuesday.

Markets were quick to take note of the announcement, and Mercedes shares dropped 3.4% in trading on Tuesday morning.

The move makes Mercedes the third big German carmaker to lower its outlook for 2026 after BMW and VW took similar steps.

Mercedes-Benz CEO Ola Kaellenius has called on German employees to work more without pay while also expanding manufacturing operations in Hungary, where he said costs are about 70% lower than in Germany.

Mercedes currently expects an adjusted car profit margin of 2% to 3% in 2026, compared to the 3% to 5% in the previous guidance.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

Like many German automakers, Mercedes has faced weak sales in China. German carmakers have struggled in the world's largest car market with sluggish demand and increased competition from local manufacturers.

Mercedes vehicle deliveries in China — last year already at their lowest level since 2016 — fell a further 29% in the nine months to the end of September.

Mercedes also released third-quarter figures earlier than planned, which showed that the company generated just €172 million ($191 million) in free cash flow from its vehicle business, down on the €422 million forecast by financial market experts.

Before interest and tax, Mercedes posted an operating profit of €1.77 billion — more than double the €750 million recorded a year earlier, according to the preliminary figures. But last year's stats were significantly impacted by one-time expenses, especially related to job cuts and legal disputes.

Adjusted for one-off items, the operating profit margin in the passenger car business stood at 2.5%, down on the 4.8% recorded a year earlier.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

The German agency responsible for finding a final repository for nuclear waste (BGE) has eliminated five states from its search.

Berlin, Hesse, Rhineland-Palatinate, Saxony and Saarland were deemed unsuitable for long-term radioactive waste storage.

In a report issued Tuesday, the BGE said it had limited its search to 5% of Germany, down from 25% in 2025. The federal agency aims to suggest suitable locations for final evaluation by the end of 2027.

Regions in northern, northwestern, southern and eastern Germany remain under consideration as locations for final storage facilities.

Germany's nuclear waste is currently stored in 16 above-ground interim storage facilities.

The BGE assessments evaluate regions' geological conditions and their ability to safely contain highly radioactive material. Granite, salt, and clay are generally considered potentially suitable types of rock and areas with damaged or compromised subsurface conditions, places with mines or volcanos have been active, are not eligible as final disposal sites.

Germany needs to find a repository for approximately 27,000 cubic meters of highly radioactive nuclear waste generated over more than 60 years of nuclear power generation. The site is expected to ensure safety for 1 million years. The last German nuclear power plants were decommissioned in April 2023.

BGE said its goal remains finding the site that offers the highest level of safety for highly radioactive waste.

The agency's recommendations, however, are not legally binding and it will be up to German lawmakers to determine the final disposal site.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

Convicted right-wing terrorist Beate Zschäpe's request for early release from prison was denied with a court ruling that she would remain behind bars for at least nine more years.

Munich's Higher Regional Court on Tuesday set her minimum term at at least 24 years and refused to suspend the sentence to probation. By determining her guilt to be particularly severe, the court effectively ruled out her release after 15 years, which, including her time in pretrial detention, would have expired this year.

The Munich court said Zschäpe, currently 51, still had a good chance of leaving prison alive.

The decision is not yet legally binding, and the defense and the Federal Prosecutor's Office can appeal.

Zschäpe had been sentenced to life in prison in 2018 as an accomplice in the National Socialist Underground (NSU) murders that killed 10 people, mainly individuals with an immigrant background as well as a police officer.

The terror group went undetected for a decade. Zschäpe's fellow NSU members, Uwe Mundlos and Uwe Böhnhardt, injured several people with bomb attacks in Cologne and killed themselves to avoid arrest in 2011.

Under normal conditions, a convict who receives a life sentence in Germany can apply for parole after 15 years.

Bayern Munich striker Harry Kane has won football's most prestigious individual prize, beating Kylian Mbappe and Lamine Yamal. Kane has developed even more in the Bundesliga despite an uneven league.

German Defense Minister Boris Pistorius, along with his counterparts from France, Italy, Poland and the UK, authored an op-ed calling Russia "the most acute and long-term threat to Euro-Atlantic security and stability."

In the article, published online and in Tuesday's Tagesspiegel newspaper, the defense ministers wrote they "share a deep conviction" that European countries need to do more to ensure their own security and aim to build "a stronger Europe within a stronger NATO."

The ministers, however, added that the United States would remain an "indispensable ally."

The pronouncement comes as many in Europe are wary of US President Donald Trump's commitment to the NATO military alliance.

The US leader has threatened to leave the group and to seize control of Greenland, a territory of fellow NATO member Denmark. US presidents have repeatedly called for European NATO members to contribute more to the alliance's military capabilities.

As US support for Ukraine also appears to waver, the five defense ministers reiterated their political, military and financial support for Kyiv as it fights of Russia's full-scale invasion.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

In Singapore, to start a four-day business-oriented trip that will also bring him to Japan and South Korea, Chancellor Friedrich Merz said it was up to European and Asian nations to find their spot amid a changing global order.

"We must assert our interests in an international environment shaped by renewed great-power rivalry," Merz said.

With a view to unpredictable tariffs imposed by the United States under President Donald Trump and trade restrictions from China, Merz emphasized the stability offered by Germany and the rest of Europe.

"This is a deliberate counterpoint to what we are currently seeing. We want to do things differently, and we want to show that there is a better way," Merz said, adding that Europe sought to expand partnerships to increase free trade with open competition, reliability and a rules-based order.

He also called for increased international investment and cooperation.

"Under the federal government I lead, investment opportunities will be continuously improved," Merz said following a meeting with Singapore Prime Minister Lawrence Wong. "I encounter a great deal of confidence here in Germany and in Europe as locations for investment."

The German leader called for a new free-trade agreement between the 27-member European Union and the Trans-Pacific Partnership (CPTPP), comprising 12 countries across five continents, including Australia, Canada, Japan, Mexico and the United Kingdom. Neither the United States nor China is part of the CPTPP.

For his part, Wong said investment in Germany and Europe would continue.

"Many of our investors, including our sovereign wealth funds, have been investing in Germany for a long time," Wong said. "They will continue to invest because they are confident that, in the long term, Germany and Europe have potential."

Merz and Wong agreed their nations would work to expand cooperation in security and defense as well as trade, investment, sustainable energy and artificial intelligence.

Guten Morgen and welcome to our daily coverage of what's making news in Germany.

While we follow the news here in Berlin and Bonn, German Chancellor Friedrich Merz is in Singapore, speaking about international cooperation among middle-power countries in Europe and Asia amid a "renewed great-power rivalry."

Today, we're also expecting a decision on whether to proceed with a case against a Nord Stream sabotage suspect and a report on Germany's ongoing search for a nuclear waste storage facility.

Not to mention a car ramming last night near the northern German city of Hannover that has left several people with serious injuries, while the suspects are still on the run.
